mappings.note: PARTIAL FIT. (a) Dalton's postulates match no outcome - the V25 hole. (b) asks how later discoveries modified them, which is CG7's 'Science is ever evolving', and the modification itself is the existence of the subatomic particles (LO-1). V25 asks only (a) and so drops to CG1; the added (b) is what earns a real code here.

Third member of the notation-numerical family with P13 and N11: read A and Z off the superscript and subscript (LO-6) and then take n = 31 - 15 (LO-4). L95, which states its numbers in words, gets LO-4 alone.
Plain n = A - Z on helium, numbers given in words - LO-4 alone, as at P11 and N12. (Item quality note, not a curriculum issue: the stem says 'atomic mass of 4u' but uses it as the mass number.)

Needs the capacities of K and L (LO-5's 'maximum number of electrons in a shell') laid over LO-2's shell scheme to total 10. Stops there, which is the split from C117, which takes the same premise on to naming the element and its valency.

The bare calculation twin of S76 and C88: a 3:1 abundance weighted onto 35 u and 37 u (LO-5's 'interpret data, such as atomic mass') over LO-3's atomic mass and isotopes. No explanation of the result is asked for, but the codes are the same - no legal code distinguishes the calculation from its interpretation.

POOR FIT, fourth parmanu item and mapped as O1, V24 and S54. C5.1 is on slightly firmer ground here than elsewhere because the stem is built around an ancient MANUSCRIPT, i.e. literature, influencing science. The Dalton half of the item falls in the same hole recorded at V25 - no outcome states his theory.

Three parts, three codes: p, n and e from Z = 13 and A = 27 (LO-4); the atomic-number versus mass-number distinction (LO-3); and the valency, which requires 2,8,3 to be built first (LO-2). Fuller than S61, which contrasts the two numbers and stops.

PARTIAL FIT. (a) asks for a schematic of the EXPERIMENT - source, foil, screen - not of an atomic model, so LO-28's diagram clause does not reach it any more than it reaches L85's cathode-ray tube. (b) and (c) are observations and the nuclear conclusion, which is LO-1's charge and position.

(a) is LO-3 - isotopes, and identical chemistry from identical valence electrons - and (b) is the abundance-weighted average, LO-5's atomic-mass interpretation. Same pair as P18, S67, S76 and L97; this item simply asks both halves.

Parts 1 to 3 are pure LO-1 - equal and opposite charges giving neutrality, electrons embedded in the positive sphere. Part 4 asks outright why the model was superseded, which is the CG7 trigger I have applied consistently (P5, N5, O13, V26, S75): cite it when the replacement IS the answer.

PARTIAL FIT, the cyclist-analogy version of N10, L84 and C112 and mapped identically. Only the discrete-orbit idea is reachable, through LO-2; the radiating-accelerated-charge physics that the whole analogy is built on is in no outcome, and C1.1 is the only intact row naming Bohr's model.

Identifying sodium and chlorine from Z = 11 and Z = 17 is LO-5's classification clause; the octet term and the two valencies are LO-3. No LO-2 here, unlike C107 - the stem already hands over the outer-shell counts as 'tokens in the outermost ring', so no configuration has to be built.

(a) is the isotope definition (LO-3), but (b) and (c) are iodine-131 in thyroid treatment and two further uses, which is the applications hole recorded at V49, S68 and L92 - only CG5's cross-curricular linkage reaches a medical use.

Same pair as V51 plus a calculation: why no single atom can weigh 35.5 u (whole nucleons), what the two isotopic forms are (LO-3), and the weighted average (LO-5). LO-4 was considered for the whole-nucleon argument but nothing is actually counted from A and Z, so it stays out.

Two asks that match two different clauses: 2n-squared for the seating capacities is LO-5's 'maximum number of electrons in a shell', and 'can the third circle fill early' is LO-2's stepwise inner-to-outer distribution, the V43 rule. The only item in the chapter that tests both capacity and filling order together.

Configurations of Mg and O built from Z (LO-2), then lose-or-gain and valency read off them (LO-3). Mapped identically to S63 and L91, which are the same task on the same or neighbouring elements - a family that honestly shares one pair, and I have not invented a distinction between them.

PARTIAL FIT. Name and location of the neutron are LO-1's charge and position clauses exactly. The other two parts - its mass against a proton's and how it resolved the atomic-mass discrepancy - fall in the mass gap noted at V35, S70 and S82, and the 1932 discovery is the history gap from V34.

Element X's Z = 13 and A = 13 + 14 and element Y's neutron count are LO-4; part (a), naming the light outer particles as electrons, is LO-1's position clause. The 'negligible mass' framing the whole scenario rests on is, once again, in no outcome.

The isobar term is LO-3, and then both neutron counts have to be produced from A - Z (LO-4). That second step is what separates this from V52 and V53, which define isobars or name the Ar/Ca pair without computing anything.

The best-fitting member of the Bohr family, because part 3 asks how the orbits are DENOTED and the answer is K, L, M, N - LO-2's own wording - rather than a postulate. C1.1 still carries the model attribution, and the no-radiation clause in part 2 remains uncovered.

Writing the carbon atom as mass-number-over-atomic-number is the international convention (LO-6), A = 6 + 6 is LO-4, and what Z represents is LO-3. The fourth part - the charge left after losing an electron - would be LO-1 and is the strand the three-code cap costs; it carries one of four marks.

Capacities of K, L and M by 2n-squared (LO-5), the 2,8,1 distribution (LO-2) and the valence-electron count (LO-3). Part 1, protons equal electrons, would be LO-4 and is the strand dropped to the cap, being the smallest of the four.

LO-3 defines isotopes and explains the identical chemistry, while producing A = 1, 2 and 3 for protium, deuterium and tritium from the given p and n is LO-4. V48 asks only what hydrogen's isotopes share and gets LO-3 alone - the arithmetic is what adds LO-4 here.

Neutron counts for Ar-40 and Ca-40 from A - Z (LO-4), then the isobar definition and verdict (LO-3). Same pair as C111 on the same pair of elements; the two items are honestly the same task and I have not split them.

Shell capacities and the 2,8 total (LO-2 with LO-5's maximum clause), then naming neon from Z = 10 - LO-5's 'classify elements accurately' - and predicting zero valency (LO-3). L96 shares the premise but stops at the total, which is why it carries two codes and this carries three.
